draft_evidence.quote:
The wall, timber on a stone footing, the same. The bowman on the gate-walk, the same man, who looked down at six where he had seen six go out and called nothing, which was his whole vocabulary and was enough. The yard, the well, the grain loft with its ladder, the house with two chimneys and one of them smoking. The steading's woman at the house door with her arms folded, counting them as they came in the way he was counting her steading, and arriving at the same number, and looking at Lira's arm slung across her chest, and at Karis's throat, and at the mule with its three boxes, and saying, "Six. Well," which was a ledger line.

Lira had walked the two days the way Oryn told her and not the way she walked, which was the first time in four years he had seen her take an order about her own body and keep it past the first mile. She stopped inside the gate and did not sit down until Oryn said she could.

comparison_evidence.quote: *Injuries, all six, after Oryn's morning. Lira: left arm slung, second day, not used for anything — she ate with the right and let me tape the ankle; Oryn says holding. Karis: throat mended, voice none; Oryn says days, and hoarse before it's anything. Brom: right hand closed, four lines across the pads, nothing on the string for three days. Me: right calf washed and bound, not mended; nothing under her hands, the fourth time; closing on its own, faster than it should. Ribs, tape twenty-one days. Oryn: three mendings in two days — the arm, the throat, the hand — and she says that's a route, and the route's eleven days north. Seln: nothing.*

findings.consequence: A full-draft exact search for 'ankle' returns zero, and every Brom appearance in Chapter 13 omits his hand and the three-day string restriction. Chapter 13 opens at the end of the two-day walk, while those constraints were still open at departure; the draft selectively carries Lira's arm, Karis's throat, and Cael's wounds but gives no recurrence or explicit resolution for Lira's taped right ankle or Brom's restricted bow hand at their next appearance. A careful reader or later action scene can therefore lose two pieces of recovery state.
findings.repair_target: Make Lira's taped ankle and Brom's still-active hand/string restriction recur or resolve on the page without changing the assigned acquisition scene, adding treatment, or altering any other injury state.

concerns: Taste only: the chapter uses inclusive calendar language for Cael's calf ('opened ... four days ago' / 'Closed. Four days') while the same night calls him three days off the Ring. The running-state chronology can support four named dates (96-99) but only about three elapsed days, so an audio listener may hear a one-day discrepancy; because the series often counts named days inclusively and the packet itself says three days off deployment, this is not promoted to a verified finding.

Taste only: the long reading names each of the nine fragments in sequence. The catalogue suits Cael and makes the full-architecture pass legible, but the Wind-through-Blade inventory slightly slows the clinical mystery before Oryn's fixed failure report; a later compression pass could test whether every named stop earns its audio time without removing the whole-of-him sensation.

Taste only: 'the ones she had touched settling differently' brushes close to the packet's prohibition on staging destabilization before Chapter 14. In context it describes the immediate tactile effect of Oryn's ongoing reading before acquisition, not the post-acquisition listening/destabilization sequence reserved for Chapter 14, so the stronger reading is compliant. Preserve that boundary in any revision.
strengths: Yes: worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. Thornwater is counted by returns, injuries change pace and posture, Tide medicine operates through hands, time, reserve, privacy, sleep, food, route debt, and professional limits, and the system's new clinical category emerges because it must classify an actual ethical/medical event.

There is no fight, exactly as prohibited, so no combat win sentence of the form 'X removed Y's ability to Z' applies. The deep-reading set piece is memorable and mechanically choreographed: the shut door makes consent/privacy pressure inescapable, sternum-and-spine contact fixes the geometry, the east-window light times the twenty minutes, Oryn's current moves fragment by fragment, and the turn occurs when Cael declines the available ways to stop it. Its outcome sentence is: Cael removes his own ability to pretend the acquisition was accidental by writing the price before contact and admitting afterward, 'No. I did.'

The covenant council earns the acquisition ethically without pretending to solve the ethics. Lira distinguishes reading from taking, Brom asks who bears the unpriced cost, Seln separates requested examination from informed consent, Karis extends earnest/non-hostile to real/non-fight, and Cael records both his best argument and his fear before choosing.

Oryn's failure to read is disciplined. She reports movement, uncertainty, missing edges, and inability to find banks; she never converts an instrument limit into an ontological claim. The fixed twenty-minute report therefore expands wonder while protecting the Book 8 reveal boundary.

The sensation of the reading is specific to both viewpoint and profession: cold without temperature, a hand learning a rope's lay, current going along rather than down, Shadow quieting under touch, and sunlight serving as clock. Cael remains a cataloguer even through unprecedented intimacy.

The notice is cleanly owned, triggered, state-consistent, and speakable. Its two public firsts—clinical engagement and a fragment that does nothing in a fight—advance visible progression and the book's human argument together; the private third count activates the five-year anomaly without explaining it.

The final exchange lands changed pressure rather than summary. Oryn detects the change, Cael accepts authorship, disclosure becomes unavoidable, and her dry twenty-one-minute order preserves clinical authority while carrying the ethical consequence into Chapter 14. It also differs cleanly from Chapter 12's image ending.

Production hygiene is strong: 5,169 words is within tolerance; section 8.4 metadata and summary greps are zero; every capped tic is zero in Chapter 13 and within the Book 7 cap; attribution survives audio; names are established and aurally distinct; the prohibited pitch and modern registers are absent; and all fixed dialogue and notice text is exact.
